column12: The social challenge I care about the most is the world bashing people who are themselves or who try to be themselves. column9: I'm majoring in Forensic Science and Data Science Analytics & Visualization at Chaminade University of Honolulu. I chose the forensic science beachside. Growing up, I knew I wanted to work in law enforcement, but I didn’t want to sit behind a desk all day. I wanted to do something with the science department, and forensic science was the best choice. I chose to major in Data Science because I had two very eye-opening experiences this past summer, one with SPICE and the other with ACSC. Before coming to Chaminade, I didn’t know what data science was or what it entailed, but through these two programs, I learned new skills and knowledge that I can connect to my current forensics major and use in another job later on. Forensics isn’t my end goal. So, I chose Chaminade University because it had the major I wanted and was close to home. Helping my family save on costs helps my mental health and well-being. I learned from traveling for softball that I don't want to travel outside my state. I’m very grounded here and in my community. Chaminade University gave me the best of both worlds, allowing me to study what I wanted from home.
column10: Growing up, I watched a lot of Criminal Minds, NCIS, CSI, and different true crime documentaries. I also found their work very interesting, and sitting in front of that TV watching Abby from NCIS inspired me to go into forensics. I like puzzles and games where I must strategize and outthink others together. I didn't think a police officer or government agent would be the best job for me because I don't want to be put into those highly hostile situations or go into the field and have discussions that could affect many people's lives. A CSI or lab person would be a better fit because I still contribute to many high-profile cases, allowing me to find, process, and provide evidence. I can do all the back work by proving facts, which are key in any case that occurs, because without the work of a forensic scientist, all you have is theory and allegations. You don't have anything concrete, which makes my job so much more important, which is why growing up, I really wanted to be a CSI or a specialized forensic technician.
column11: If I could design my invention, I would create an extensive X-ray. I know that X-rays already exist, but I would make one on a much larger scale that could scan large vehicles like trucks, planes, coaches, etc. I would do this to help identify objects or people who should otherwise not be there. The amount of illegal objects or people transported is unimaginable. Because we don’t have the right resources or due to ethical concerns, we don’t have the right system in place to entirely prevent situations like these from happening. With this a-ray, we would be able to identify more suspicious activity and question the contents of each vehicle. Hoping to catch more suspicious behavior or illegal activity faster and at a higher rate.
column12: The societal challenge I care most about is vehicle accident prevention. Recently, a high spike in vehicle crash accidents in Hawaii has occurred. Ending in critical or lethal conditions for the individual involved. It’s to the point where we have some injured from a vehicle accident almost every single day. This is such a sad situation because not many plan to get into a crash; it all depends on the circumstances that occur, which could position you at the place of the accident. This issue is also very prevalent in other areas, not just in Hawaii, and will continue because it is an issue until a solution is reached. No solution will be perfect, but if we can do more to prevent the challenge, things will improve.
column13: The best advice I received in college was, Always be unapologetically yourself. This resonated with me because I’m very passive, so I will adapt to my environment and form something new. Presentation for myself to fit in. Doing this, I began to lose myself by constantly trying to be what others needed me to be. I've always been scared to show others who I really am, in fear of being disliked or rejected, which really messed with my mental/emotional health. The toll it took affected me a lot more than I noticed, and started to affect how I operated in my day-to-day life. One of my closest friends, whom I talked to, told me I should be unapologetically myself, because who am I if not myself? I am who I am, and I gotta own my person. If I keep fearing what others might think or changing myself to others' needs, I'm not truly living. I should be confident and proud of who I am, and the people who will stay with me because of that are my true friends/people. I can’t please everyone, so the best I can do is be myself.
column14: I don’t think most people know how time-consuming forensics work really is. We have to take many tedious steps to ensure the integrity of the crime scene and evidence. Due to so many laws and regulations on how things need to be done, wheat needs to be collected, and documentation that needs to be filled out, it will take a very long time. In movies, it shows work that can take up to two months or more, but is put into a three-day process. It’s not very realistic, but so many people watch it and are influenced by what they see that they don’t realize how inaccurate a lot of the information is, because this is the only side they are exposed to. The amount of work needed is so tremendous that it could make or break a case or result in nothing. If there's one thing I want people to know, fore ocs is a lot of work. I want everyone to appreciate everything that they do truly.

column9: I grew up with critical Asian parents, who monitored my social media accounts. This, however, sparked my interest in Computer Science: to evade my father's surveillance, I resolved to create a website that belonged only to me. First, it was a basic collection of local files, lacking any design or aesthetic appeal. However, by learning to use GitHub and leveraging open-source resources, I began to transform it into something I could be proud of. Scrolling through my personal blog, for the first time, I felt a profound sense of amazement and relief that I could actually create something. After that, I felt unstoppable, and I wanted to see what more I could do and how far I could go with Computer Science.

column14: In Large language Model training, the numbers of credible resources that an Artificial Intelligence gives grow linearly as the amount of input questions gets larger; however, the false information it gives grows exponentially, which means it will cooperate with related resources and come up with new and unreliable information, and these will be more than the actuated ones. Instead of checking AI’s answer at the beginning and building trust, it’s better to check the answers after 10 questions, then determine if you should continue to use this Artificial Intelligence.
